reason: A opens with the Zong killings rendered scene by scene and dated, so a general reader is pulled through a concrete sequence before the argument arrives, and the later sections (Barbados code, Jamaican ledgers, Toussaint, Dessalines, Louisiana) keep handing the chapter a new place and a new actor. B is essentially one thesis restated in essay paragraphs: the Brookes diagram, the Bristol figures, the Codrington bequest and the 'economics alone cannot explain it' point return four or five times each in slightly different wording, and whole late sections (the resistance catalogue, then the economic-determinism section) recapitulate material already covered. A also moves forward chronologically and geographically, while B loops back to the same three exhibits, so A has the stronger sense of movement.
